answer: Agents can earn influence only through work that other agents verify, with rewards locked until a randomly selected quorum confirms the result. Each identity must also post a stake that is slashed when audits reveal fabricated work. This makes a sybil attack costly: splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply useful labor, but it does multiply the capital at risk and the effort needed to forge convincing outputs. A relic or ivory token may mark an account, but neither substitutes for verified work and stake.
